messages:
maria: Heads-up — planning a Terraform cutover tonight for tenant fencing + outbound routing in us-west-2. Change window 23:00-00:30 PT. Need agreement on provider pin, IAM service-account rotation, and whether we serialise by tenant.

josh: Ack. Serialising by tenant sounds safer. Recommend TF_VAR_batch_size=1 and a staggered apply per tenant tag. Keeps blast radius tiny. :+1:

anika: I’ll open a quick PR to pin the aws provider to the verified hash (sha256:abc123def). Also adding a provider_lock file change so the execution plane is consistent.

maria: Thanks. Plan I’m proposing: 1) pin provider 2) drain outgoing egress for one AZ 3) apply tenant fencing module for tenants A-D 4) smoke test 5) promote to remaining tenants. If any error, rollback to prior module commit and re-run traffic shift.

tim: Oncall here — I’ll watch metrics and have rollback steps ready. What’s the explicit rollback command we want people to run if apply fails?

maria: Rollback checklist (short):
```
# revert module version in infra-modules repo
git checkout -b revert-module-2024-11
# update root module ref to previous commit
# run terraform apply -auto-approve in staging then prod for affected tenants
```
Also: deploybot can run a state restore if needed, but we prefer module revert + selective apply.

deploybot: Scheduled terraform apply for "us-west-2 - tenant-fencing" at 2024-11-10T23:10:00Z. Plan summary: +3 to add, ~2 to change, 0 destroy. Plan output available: <redwood-ci://plans/1738254321>.

sre-oncall: I’ll keep an eye on NAT egress latency and conntrack. If we see >20% window error rate, call immediate pause.

josh: One more ask — can we set the deploybot to pause automatically between tenant groups? e.g., pause after each TF apply and wait for manual ack.

anika: I added a small change to the deploybot job config in PR #457 — it supports --pause-between-batches now and default batch=1.

maria: OK we’re ready. @deploybot kick when ready, but hold for my manual continue after the first tenant group.

deploybot: Apply started by @maria. Working directory: infra/live/us-west-2/tenants. Running: terraform init && terraform apply -auto-approve.

sre-oncall: Observed small latency blip at 23:12 during first tenant apply — 95th latency +120ms, error rate +3%. Continuing to monitor.

josh: Any signs of config drift or IAM denies?

sre-oncall: No IAM denies yet. Errors look transient.

maria: Pause apply! Seeing repeated NAT timeouts and some egress conntrack exhaustion on a small subset. Pausing all remaining batches.

deploybot: Apply paused by @maria. Current task halted mid-batch. Capturing plan artifacts and state snapshot.

anika: I opened emergency revert PR (infra-modules revert commit) and pushed a hotfix to the NAT scaling module to increase connection tracking. PR #458 ready to merge if we decide to rollback.

tim: Given the conntrack overload, I recommend rollback + re-run with nat-scaling fix in place. I can merge and trigger a controlled rollback.

maria: Go ahead with rollback. Merge PR #458, then run the rollback steps from the checklist. Notify SRE when revert apply starts.

deploybot: Rollback triggered by @tim. Running: git revert <module-commit> && terraform apply -target=module.nat_scaling -auto-approve. State restore step queued.

sre-oncall: Seeing metrics stabilise as conntrack increases. No further error rate spikes after the rollback apply started.

deploybot: Rollback apply complete. State reconciled. Notifications sent to paging list and infra-runbook updated with timestamps.

maria: Thanks everyone. We’ll capture a short postmortem and reschedule the cutover to a low-traffic weekend window after provider pin is enforced and NAT scaling validated.

josh: Good call pausing. lessons: always test conntrack at tenant scale in staging.

anika: I’ll bake the provider_lock and nat-scaling smoke tests into the CI.

maria: Closing this thread for now — follow-up postmortem + new change window TODO in #eng-releases. :memo:
